title: Cohort probe playbook and panel orchestration notes
summary: Working notes for designing a lightweight probe scheduling system and a compact dashboard layout that surfaces cohort-specific latency and cost signals without exploding cardinality.
goals: Define probe cadence heuristics for tenant cohorts to catch regressions quickly while limiting trace/metric costs
Provide concrete metric definitions that balance signal fidelity and cardinality
Sketch a dashboard layout (operator + product views) that helps correlate latency slices with KV cache warmth and model variant routing
Propose an adaptive sampling & budget algorithm operators can tune per-environment
scope: Focus on inference latency and cost attribution for multi-tenant hosted and dedicated environments. Excludes embedding-only pipelines and long-tail offline batch jobs. This is a working doc intended to be a lean, operational playbook for SREs and product observability owners.
background: We frequently see noisy dashboards when we add tenant labels + model_variant + route. Cost/trace budgets rise as we add probes to many low-traffic tenants. This playbook aims to capture heuristics to avoid signal explosion and to ensure oncall can quickly determine whether a regression is tenant-local or systemic.
proposed_metrics: inference.request_rate - unit: req/s; aggregation: sum over 1m; cardinality: tenant, route, env
inference.ttft.p50/p95/p99 - unit: ms; description: time to first token; aggregation: quantiles; cardinality: tenant, route, model_family
inference.total_latency.p95 - unit: ms; description: end-to-end request latency incl network; aggregation: quantiles; cardinality: tenant, model_variant
cache.kv_warmth_fraction - unit: ratio (0-1); description: fraction of requests served from KV cache prefix; aggregation: avg over 5m; cardinality: tenant, model_family
routing.fallback_rate - unit: pct; description: fraction of requests routed to fallback/cheaper model; aggregation: rate over 5m; cardinality: tenant, region
tenant.unit_cost_perk - unit: $/k tokens; description: amortized inference cost estimate; aggregation: sum(tokens_cost)/sum(tokens) per hour; cardinality: tenant
sessionized_first_token_time - unit: ms; description: track first-token latency per session to detect cold-start cohorts; aggregation: p95 per cohort; cardinality: tenant, session_type
probe.synthetic_latency - unit: ms; description: synthetic probe response time; aggregation: p95; cardinality: probe_id, region
metric_naming_guidelines: Keep high-cardinality labels out of raw metric names; use labels/tags instead (tenant, model_variant, region).
Prefer stable prefixes: inference.*, cache.*, routing.*, probe.* so dashboards can pivot easily.
Use explicit aggregation suffixes only in panels (e.g., .p95) to make intentions clear but keep raw metrics generic for reuse.
Document allowed labels per metric and maximum cardinality per label (e.g., tenant ~ O(1k), model_variant ~ O(10)).
trace_guidelines: Trace root should include: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_variant, route, env, probe_id (if synthetic).
Span naming: 'inference/serve', 'kv/fetch', 'kernel/compile', 'routing/decision' — keep short and consistent.
Adaptive sampling: always capture 100% of errors and 1% of successes by default; increase to 5-10% for tenants flagged by anomaly detectors.
Redact PII at ingestion and include a provenance flag so replay/debugging tools can request additional context from CS after approval.
Trace retention tiers: full traces for 7 days for high-risk tenants, 3 days for normal, aggregated logs/metrics retained longer.
Span payload limits: cap model output snapshots to 4KB in traces to avoid cost blowup; store longer artifacts in an artifact store and reference by id.
dashboard_layout_suggestions: Top row (operator view): global request_rate, global p95 ttft, probe failure_rate. Quick toggle for env (prod/staging).
Second row (tenant-slice): tenant selector + small multiples for request_rate, ttft.p95, cache.kv_warmth_fraction. Default to top 10 tenants by traffic.
Third row (variant routing): model_variant fanout chart and routing.fallback_rate per region. Include a drilldown link to trace sample list.
Cost row: unit_cost_perk sparkline per tenant and a heatmap of cost delta week-over-week to spot regressions from config changes.
Operator compact: pre-baked investigation links (open traces, open slow session replays, runbook actions) to reduce time-to-action.
Design note: prioritize small multiples over exploding panels that aggregate by too many labels; use interactive filters instead.
probe_scheduling_algorithm: Heuristic-driven adaptive scheduler: classify tenants into 3 cohorts (high, medium, low) by 7-day request volume. Probe cadence defaults: high=30s, medium=5m, low=30m. For tenants with historical instability ( > 2 regressions in 30 days) bump cadence one rung. Cap total synthetic probes per region to a budgeted QPS (operator-configurable). When a probe detects p95 above threshold, escalate: double probe frequency for affected cohort and trigger 10x sample rate for traces for the next 30m.
sampling_budget_calculator: budget_per_region = baseline_traces_per_min + sum(active_high_tenants * extra_rate). Example: baseline=5 traces/min; active_high_tenants=12 => extra_rate=0.5 traces/min each => budget=5 + 12*0.5 = 11 traces/min. Allow operators to set a hard cap per region and a soft cap that triggers rate-limiting of non-error captures.
runbook_quick_actions: If global p95 ttft jumps > 20%: check probe.synthetic_latency; if probes are stable, check routing.fallback_rate and top-k tenant sessionized_first_token_time.
If a tenant has isolated p99 regression: switch tenant to dedicated routing (if available) or pin to previous model_variant, roll back canary for that tenant.
Cache coldness pattern: if cache.kv_warmth_fraction drops by >50% for heavy tenants, trigger KV prefetch job (link to infra runbook).
Cost surge: if unit_cost_perk increases >30% week-over-week for top-5 tenants, open a cost incident and collect token-level traces for last 24h.
Probe budget breach: reduce synthetic cadence for low cohort and enable aggregated-only probes (metrics, no traces) until cap cleared.
open_questions: Should synthetic probes mirror a subset of real user prompts (privacy concerns) or use canonical lightweight probes?
What is our SLA for probe-driven escalations (target detection time from regression to alert)?
How to surface model-quantization-level signals without adding a new high-cardinality label?
Where to store full artifacts (model outputs) for debug while maintaining access controls?
decisions: Default sampling: 100% errors + 1% successes; escalate to 5-10% for signaled tenants. (tentative)
Naming policy: use stable prefixes and labels; reserve metric names under inference.*, cache.*, routing.*, probe.*.
Retention tiers: 7 days full for high-risk tenants, 3 days for regular; metrics retained per existing retention policy.
